mainTopic: רבי's final instructions and how the גמרא explains them: eulogies, mourning, his successors, רבי חייא's greatness, and רבי's last days.
overview: This amud finishes רבי's final instructions before his death and then explains them one by one. His request not to be eulogized in the small towns turns out to be about his honor, not about saving people trouble. His request to reopen the ישיבה after thirty days is modeled on the mourning for משה רבינו. A בת קול promises עולם הבא to everyone at רבי's funeral, and also to a devoted launderer who missed it and died of grief. The גמרא explains why גמליאל became נשיא even though שמעון was wiser: he matched his fathers in יראת חטא. It then tells how רבי חנינא first deferred to the older רבי אפס, and how רב worked out from לוי's arrival in בבל that רבי אפס had died. The גמרא asks why רבי חייא was not appointed and gives two answers: either he died first, or he was busy with his great work of spreading תורה to children. The amud ends with רבי's last words to his sons, advice to be warm in private and firm in public, and the start of an explanation of why רבי was moved from בֵּית שְׁעָרִים to צִיפּוֹרִי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבי's instructions: reopening the ישיבה and naming successors
steps.stepSummary: רבי finishes his instructions. The ישיבה should reopen after thirty days. שמעון his son will be the חכם, גמליאל his son will be the נשיא, and חנינא בר חמא will sit at the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: "...and reopen the ישיבה after thirty days." "My son שמעון is the חכם, my son גמליאל is the נשיא, and חנינא בר חמא will sit at the head."
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last part of רבי's instructions before he died. He tells them when to restart learning and who gets which leadership job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the closing lines of a list that began earlier on the daf. רבי divides leadership among three people instead of giving it all to one. The גמרא will soon go back and explain some of these instructions.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall, where the learning sessions take place
Sage, here a specific position of leadership
The head of the Jewish people (the נשיא)
Will sit at the head (lead the ישיבה)

phrases.english: "...and reconvene the yeshiva after thirty days."
"Shimon my son is the Sage,
Gamliel my son is the Nasi,
Chanina bar Chama will sit at the head."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of רבי's instructions that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning restarts after thirty days. Leadership is split: שמעון is חכם, גמליאל is נשיא, and חנינא בר חמא heads the ישיבה.

steps.title: First understanding: no eulogies in the towns, to save people trouble
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining 'do not eulogize me in the towns.' At first people understood it as a way to save others the bother.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Do not eulogize me in the towns.' They understood that he said this because of the bother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to one of רבי's earlier instructions and tells us how people first understood it. This sets up a change of understanding in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their first guess was that רבי was being considerate. He did not want everyone to travel around to many small eulogies. This guess will be overturned in the next step.

phrases.english: Do not eulogize me in the towns —
they understood from it
that he said it because of the bother.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבוּר מִינַּהּ מִשּׁוּם טִרְחָא הוּא דְּקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the list of instructions to explaining one of them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first reading: the request was meant to save people trouble.

steps.title: Real reason: no eulogies in the towns, for his honor
steps.stepSummary: People saw that everyone came to the eulogies in the big cities anyway. So they realized רבי's reason was honor, not saving trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they saw that the eulogies were in the big cities and everyone came, they said: learn from this that he said it because of honor.
steps.whatsHappening: Something happened that showed the first understanding was wrong, so they changed their minds about רבי's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If saving trouble were the goal, it failed, because everyone traveled to the cities anyway. So the real point must have been honor. Large gatherings in big cities fit רבי's greatness better than small eulogies in towns.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude

steps.whatToRemember: 'Don't eulogize me in the towns' was not about saving people trouble. It was about רבי's honor, so the eulogies would draw big crowds in the cities.

phrases.english: Once they saw that they were eulogizing in the big cities
and everyone was coming,
they said: learn from this
that he said it because of honor.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִשּׁוּם יְקָרָא הוּא דְּקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the first understanding (trouble) with the true reason (honor).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי asked not to be eulogized in the towns for the sake of his honor.

steps.title: Why reopen after thirty days: משה was mourned thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רבי's instruction to reopen the ישיבה after thirty days is based on the mourning for משה רבינו, which lasted thirty days according to the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Reopen the ישיבה after thirty days' — because I am no greater than משה רבינו, as it says: 'And בני ישראל wept for משה in the plains of מואב thirty days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains a second instruction. רבי gives his own reason and supports it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי compares himself to משה humbly. If משה was mourned in full for thirty days, it is not right for רבי to be mourned in full for longer. So learning should restart after thirty days.

phrases.english: Reconvene the yeshiva after thirty days —
because I am not better than Moshe our teacher,
as it is written:
"And the children of Israel wept for Moshe
in the plains of Moav thirty days,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to explaining a second instruction of רבי.
steps.raayaObject: Reopening the ישיבה after thirty days of mourning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in דברים: בני ישראל wept for משה for thirty days.

steps.title: How משה was mourned: thirty full days, then part-time for a year
steps.stepSummary: For thirty days משה was eulogized day and night. After that, they eulogized during one part of the day and learned during the other, for twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: For thirty days they eulogized day and night. From then on they eulogized by day and learned by night, or eulogized by night and learned by day, until they had eulogized for twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the thirty days for משה looked like, and what happened after them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thirty days were full-time mourning that stopped all learning. After that, mourning went on for a year, but only part-time, alongside learning. This is why רבי said learning should restart after thirty days. Mourning does not end then; it just stops blocking learning.
steps.confusionAlert: Thirty days does not mean the mourning stopped completely. Only the full-time mourning ended. Eulogies continued part-time for a whole year.
steps.whatToRemember: Mourning for משה: thirty days full-time, then part-time together with learning for twelve months. That is the model for רבי's thirty-day instruction.

phrases.english: For thirty days they eulogized by day and night;
from then on
they eulogized by day and studied by night,
or eulogized by night and studied by day,
until they had eulogized for twelve months of the year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the details of the thirty-day mourning for משה mentioned in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thirty days of full mourning, then mourning shared with learning until twelve months.

steps.title: Heavenly voice: everyone at רבי's funeral earns the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: On the day of רבי's funeral, a בת קול announced that everyone present was destined for עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the day of רבי's funeral a בת קול came out and said: Whoever was at רבי's funeral is destined for life in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about רבי's funeral. This announcement sets up the story of the launderer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The announcement shows how great רבי was: just being at his funeral earned a person עולם הבא. It also sets up the problem for someone who was not there.

keyTerms.meaning: Life in the World to Come

phrases.english: On that day of Rebbi's funeral
a heavenly voice came out and said:
Whoever was at Rebbi's funeral
is destined for life in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יוֹמָא דְּאַשְׁכָּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי נְפַקָא בַּת קָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי's instructions to a story about his funeral.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attending רבי's funeral earned a person עולם הבא.

steps.title: The launderer who missed the funeral
steps.stepSummary: A launderer who came to רבי every day missed that one day. When he heard, he went up to the roof, fell, and died.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain launderer used to come before רבי every day, but on that day he did not come. When he heard this, he went up to the roof, fell to the ground, and died.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with one man who missed the funeral, and tells how much it broke him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This man was faithful to רבי every single day, yet he missed the one day that earned עולם הבא. His grief was so great that he fell from the roof and died. The story sets up the final announcement.

phrases.english: A certain launderer
would come before him every day;
that day he did not come.
Once he heard this,
he went up to the roof
and fell to the ground and died.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא כּוֹבֵס כֹּל יוֹמָא הֲוָה אָתֵי קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces someone who was left out of the בת קול's announcement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The launderer missed the funeral and died of grief.

steps.title: Heavenly voice: the launderer too earns the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: A second בת קול announced that the launderer also was destined for עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת קול came out and said: That launderer too is destined for life in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. Heaven announces that the launderer was included after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first announcement covered only those who were present. This second announcement adds the launderer, even though he missed the funeral. His deep devotion and grief over רבי counted for him.
steps.whatToRemember: The launderer who missed רבי's funeral and died of grief was also promised עולם הבא.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
That launderer too
is destined for life in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף הַהוּא כּוֹבֵס מְזוּמָּן הוּא לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the launderer's story by including him in the promise of the first בת קול.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The launderer was also destined for עולם הבא.

steps.title: What did רבי mean by 'My son שמעון is wise'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from רבי's instructions and asks what he meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'My son שמעון is a חכם' — what was he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a phrase from רבי's instructions before he died and asks what it means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken alone, the line sounds like a compliment with no point. The גמרא wants to know why רבי said it as part of his instructions about who would lead.

keyTerms.meaning: A wise person, a Torah scholar
What is he saying? (asking for the meaning of a statement)

phrases.english: My son Shimon is a Sage —
what was he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of רבי's funeral back to the content of his final instructions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The intended meaning of 'שמעון בני חכם' in רבי's instructions.

steps.title: Even though שמעון is wiser, גמליאל should be נשיא
steps.stepSummary: רבי meant that גמליאל gets the נשיאות even though שמעון is the greater scholar.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he was saying: even though my son שמעון is wise, my son גמליאל should be the נשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the two halves of רבי's statement belong together: even though שמעון is wiser, גמליאל becomes נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line about שמעון's wisdom is not a separate compliment. It prevents anyone from arguing that the wiser son should lead. רבי is making it clear that wisdom alone does not decide who gets the position.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he was saying (introduces an explanation)
The head of the Jewish people and the סנהדרין

phrases.english: This is what he was saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשִּׁמְעוֹן בְּנִי חָכָם,
phrases.english: Although my son Shimon is a Sage,
my son Gamliel should be the Nasi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two parts of the statement are one thought: despite שמעון's greater wisdom, גמליאל is appointed נשיא.

steps.title: לוי asks why this needed to be said
steps.stepSummary: לוי questions why רבי had to give this instruction at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי said: Does this need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: לוי challenges the instruction itself. He asks why רבי had to say this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי assumes the answer is obvious. גמליאל was the firstborn, and as step 13 will show, the firstborn normally inherits his father's position. So why would רבי need to spell it out?

keyTerms.meaning: A student and colleague of רבי
Does it need to be said? (implying it is obvious)

phrases.english: Levi said: Does this need to be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the instruction explained in step 10 was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's instruction that גמליאל be נשיא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the firstborn inherits anyway, the instruction adds nothing.

steps.title: רבי שמעון sharply rejects לוי's question
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון, the son of רבי, tells לוי that it did need to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון the son of רבי said: It is needed for you and your limp.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון pushes back hard against לוי. He insists the instruction was necessary, but he does not say why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reply is a sharp put-down rather than an explanation. It only claims that the instruction was needed, which leaves the גמרא to work out what was wrong with לוי's question.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, said:
It is necessary for you and for your limp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers לוי's challenge from step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the instruction was unnecessary.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated; the גמרא will look for it in the next steps.

steps.title: לוי's question seems correct based on a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what bothered רבי שמעון, since a פסוק shows the firstborn inherits the kingdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was difficult for him? Doesn't the פסוק say: 'And the kingdom he gave to יהורם because he was the firstborn'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון objected, because לוי's point seems to have a source in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says יהושפט gave the kingdom to יהורם because he was the firstborn. That makes firstborn succession sound automatic. If so, לוי was right that רבי had no need to say it.

phrases.english: What did he find difficult?
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי שמעון. Why did he think לוי's question was wrong?

phrases.english: Doesn't the verse say:
"But the kingdom he gave to Jehoram
because he was the firstborn"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי שמעון's answer in step 12 by supporting לוי's question with a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's claim that the instruction was necessary
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows the firstborn inherits the kingship, so the instruction should be unnecessary.

steps.title: יהורם filled his fathers' place, but גמליאל did not
steps.stepSummary: The firstborn inherits automatically only if he is equal to his fathers. גמליאל was not, so רבי had to say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one, יהורם, filled the place of his fathers. But רבן גמליאל did not fill the place of his fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is about a firstborn who matched his fathers. גמליאל did not match them, so his appointment was not automatic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the rule of the פסוק. A firstborn inherits automatically only when he fills his fathers' place. Since גמליאל fell short, רבי needed to give an explicit instruction.

keyTerms.meaning: Fills the place of his fathers, meaning he is their equal
A king of יהודה, son of יהושפט

phrases.english: That one, Jehoram, filled the place of his fathers,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אֵינוֹ מְמַלֵּא מְקוֹם אֲבוֹתָיו הֲוָה.
phrases.english: but Rabban Gamliel did not fill the place of his fathers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A firstborn always inherits automatically, as the פסוק suggests.
steps.terutzMaskana: A firstborn inherits automatically only if he matches his fathers. גמליאל did not, so an explicit instruction was needed.

steps.title: Then why did רבי choose גמליאל at all?
steps.stepSummary: If גמליאל did not fill his fathers' place, why did רבי appoint him?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what was רבי's reason for doing this?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in step 14 creates a new problem. If גמליאל was not equal to his fathers, why did רבי pick him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 explained why an instruction was needed, but it made גמליאל sound less than qualified. The גמרא now asks what justified choosing him over the wiser שמעון.

phrases.english: And what was Rabbi's reason for doing this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of step 14's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who does not fill his fathers' place seems unfit to be appointed נשיא.

steps.title: גמליאל matched his fathers in fear of sin
steps.stepSummary: גמליאל was not equal to his fathers in wisdom, but he was equal to them in יראת חטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, he did not fill his fathers' place in wisdom. But in fear of sin he did fill his fathers' place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that גמליאל fell short only in wisdom. In fear of sin he was fully equal to his fathers, and that is why רבי chose him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'filling his fathers' place' is split into two areas: wisdom and fear of sin. גמליאל lacked only the first. His יראת חטא made him fit to be נשיא, though his weaker wisdom still meant רבי had to give a clear instruction.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי appointed גמליאל because he matched his fathers in fear of sin, even though שמעון was wiser. Since גמליאל did not match them in wisdom, his appointment was not automatic, which explains why רבי had to state it.

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי דְּאֵינוֹ מְמַלֵּא מְקוֹם אֲבוֹתָיו בְּחׇכְמָה —
phrases.english: Granted that he did not fill the place of his fathers in wisdom —

phrases.aramaic: בְּיִרְאַת חֵטְא מְמַלֵּא מְקוֹם אֲבוֹתָיו הֲוָה.
phrases.english: in fear of sin he did fill the place of his fathers.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דְּאֵינוֹ מְמַלֵּא מְקוֹם אֲבוֹתָיו בְּחׇכְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the concept into two areas
steps.terutzHavaAmina: גמליאל was entirely unequal to his fathers and so unfit.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was unequal only in wisdom. In יראת חטא he was equal, which made him fit to be נשיא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that for leadership, fear of sin can count as much as being the greatest scholar.

steps.title: רבי appoints רבי חנינא, but he refuses
steps.stepSummary: רבי instructs that חנינא בר חמא should head the ישיבה. רבי חנינא declines because רבי אפס is two and a half years older.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: חנינא בר חמא will sit at the head. But רבי חנינא did not accept, because רבי אפס was two and a half years older than him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last item on רבי's list of instructions from step 1, which names רבי חנינא בר חמא as head of the ישיבה. It then tells us that רבי חנינא turned the job down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's reason is only respect for age. רבי אפס was two and a half years older, and רבי חנינא did not want to be placed ahead of him.

keyTerms.meaning: Will sit at the head, meaning he will lead the ישיבה
He did not accept the appointment

phrases.english: Chanina bar Chama will sit at the head
Rabbi Chanina did not accept,
because Rabbi Afes was older than him
by two and a half years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי's instruction about גמליאל to his instruction about the head of the ישיבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי appointed רבי חנינא as head, but רבי חנינא deferred to the older רבי אפס.

steps.title: רבי אפס leads, and רבי חנינא and לוי sit outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי אפס sat at the head. רבי חנינא sat outside, and לוי came and sat with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אפס sat at the head, and רבי חנינא sat outside. לוי came and sat with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the seating arrangement that resulted from רבי חנינא's refusal. This sets up the next part of the story about לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא would not lead ahead of רבי אפס, but he also did not sit in front of him as a student, so he sat outside. לוי chose to learn with רבי חנינא, and that detail matters later.

phrases.english: Rabbi Afes sat at the head
and Rabbi Chanina sat outside,
phrases.notes: He means outside the ישיבה, so he would not sit as a student in front of רבי אפס.

phrases.english: and Levi came and sat with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of רבי חנינא's refusal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אפס led the ישיבה, while רבי חנינא learned outside together with לוי.

steps.title: רבי אפס dies and לוי moves to בבל
steps.stepSummary: After רבי אפס died, רבי חנינא took the head seat. לוי had no one to learn with, so he went to בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אפס died, and רבי חנינא sat at the head. לוי had no one to sit with, so he came to בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward: רבי אפס passes away and רבי חנינא finally becomes head. לוי loses his learning partner and leaves for בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבי חנינא moved inside to lead, לוי was left alone outside. That explains why לוי left ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: He passed away (literally, his soul rested)
Someone to sit and learn with

phrases.english: Rabbi Afes died
and Rabbi Chanina sat at the head,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְלֵוִי אִינִישׁ לְמֵיתַב גַּבֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: and Levi did not have anyone to sit with,
and so he came to Babylonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the seating arrangement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא became head after רבי אפס died, and לוי left for בבל.

steps.title: רב is told that a great man arrived in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: This connects to a known story: people told רב that a great man who limps had come to נהרדעא and taught that a כלילא is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they told רב: a great man came to נהרדעא. He limps, and he taught that a כלילא is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא links לוי's move to a well-known report given to רב. This sets up רב's conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report does not say who the visitor was. It gives only clues: he is a great scholar, he limps, and he ruled leniently about a כלילא.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is (what is meant by)
A crown-like ornament worn by a woman

phrases.english: And this is what they said to Rav:
A great man came to Neharde'a, and he limps,
and he taught: a kelila is permitted.
phrases.notes: He ruled that a woman may go out wearing this ornament on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects לוי's arrival in בבל to the report given to רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב was told that a great scholar who limps had come to נהרדעא and permitted a כלילא.

steps.title: רב deduces what happened in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: From the visitor's arrival, רב concluded that רבי אפס had died, רבי חנינא had become head, and לוי had come because he had no one to learn with.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Learn from this that רבי אפס died, רבי חנינא sat at the head, and לוי had no one to sit with, so he came here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב uses the visitor's arrival as evidence. He works out the whole chain of events in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב recognized the visitor as לוי. Since לוי had been learning outside with רבי חנינא, his leaving meant that רבי חנינא was no longer outside. רב concluded that רבי חנינא must have become head because רבי אפס had died.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, conclude from this

phrases.english: He said: Conclude from this
that Rabbi Afes died,
and Rabbi Chanina sat at the head,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְלֵוִי אִינִישׁ לְמֵיתַב גַּבֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: and Levi did not have anyone to sit with,
and so he came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב draws a conclusion from the report in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אפס died and רבי חנינא became head.

steps.title: Maybe רבי חנינא was the one who died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's conclusion: perhaps רבי חנינא died, רבי אפס stayed on as head, and that is why לוי was left alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead that רבי חנינא died and רבי אפס kept his seat. Then too, לוי would have had no one to sit with, and he would have come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how רב knew who had died. Another version of events would also explain why לוי came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי would lose his partner either way: if רבי חנינא moved inside, or if רבי חנינא died. So לוי's arrival alone does not prove that רבי אפס was the one who died.

keyTerms.meaning: He kept sitting as he had sat

phrases.english: But say that Rabbi Chanina died
and Rabbi Afes sat as he had sat,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְלֵוִי אִינִישׁ לְמֵיתַב גַּבֵּיהּ
phrases.english: and Levi did not have anyone to sit with
and so he came?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's deduction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's conclusion that רבי אפס died.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another scenario explains the same evidence equally well.

steps.title: לוי would have learned under רבי אפס
steps.stepSummary: First answer: לוי was willing to submit to רבי אפס. If רבי חנינא had died, לוי would simply have learned under רבי אפס and stayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: לוי would bow to רבי אפס's authority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב's conclusion. לוי had no problem learning under רבי אפס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי sat outside only to keep רבי חנינא company. If רבי חנינא had died, לוי would have gone inside and learned from רבי אפס, so he would not have needed to leave. His leaving therefore shows that רבי אפס was the one who died.

keyTerms.meaning: He would truly submit to him

phrases.english: If you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: לֵוִי לְרַבִּי אַפָּס מִיכָּף הֲוָה כַּיִיף לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Levi was subordinate to Rabbi Afes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rules out the other scenario based on לוי's relationship with רבי אפס.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוי would leave if either רבי died.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי would have stayed under רבי אפס, so רבי אפס must be the one who died.

steps.title: רבי's word had to come true
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: since רבי said that רבי חנינא would sit at the head, he had to rule eventually. A צדיק's decree comes true.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or say: since רבי said 'רבי חנינא בר חמא will sit at the head,' it is impossible that he would not rule. As it is written about the righteous: 'You will decree a thing, and it will be fulfilled for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. רבי's statement guaranteed that רבי חנינא would become head, so he could not have died first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not depend on לוי at all. It relies on the idea that a צדיק's words come true, which is learned from a פסוק. רבי חנינא had to outlive רבי אפס.

keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible that not, it must be that
You will decree, and it will be fulfilled for you

steps.whatToRemember: רב knew that רבי אפס died, either because לוי would have stayed under רבי אפס, or because רבי's appointment of רבי חנינא had to come true.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר ״רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר חָמָא יֵשֵׁב בָּרֹאשׁ״ —
phrases.english: since he said, 'Rabbi Chanina bar Chama will sit at the head,'
it is impossible that he will not rule,
as it is written about the righteous:
'You shall decree a thing, and it shall be established for you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relies on a פסוק to show that רבי's word must come true.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא might have died before leading.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי's decree guaranteed that רבי חנינא would rule, so רבי אפס died first.

steps.title: Why not appoint רבי חייא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי did not make רבי חייא the head instead of רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי חייא was there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short, sharp question. רבי חייא was a great scholar, so why did רבי choose רבי חנינא as head of the ישיבה instead of him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps assumed that רבי חנינא was the natural choice to lead. If רבי חייא was alive and available, he should have been considered first. The challenge is to the choice of leader.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But wasn't Rabbi Ḥiyya there!
phrases.notes: He means: why didn't רבי appoint רבי חייא as head instead of רבי חנינא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the choice of רבי חנינא, which steps 23-24 assumed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's appointment of רבי חנינא as head
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא was greater or more suitable, so he should have been chosen.

steps.title: רבי חייא had already died
steps.stepSummary: Answer: רבי חייא died before רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חייא could not be appointed because he died before רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple factual answer. If רבי חייא was no longer alive, there was no choice to make between him and רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: His soul rested; he passed away

phrases.english: He had died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual answer: the person in question was no longer alive
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא was available and was passed over.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא died before רבי, so he could not be appointed.

steps.title: רבי חייא saw רבי's grave
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: רבי חייא said he cried at רבי's grave, so he outlived רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי חייא say: I saw the grave of רבי and shed tears over it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. רבי חייא himself said he visited רבי's grave, so he must have been alive after רבי died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person cannot cry at the grave of someone who outlived him. This statement directly contradicts the claim that רבי חייא died first.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ḥiyya say:
I saw the grave of Rabbi,
and I shed tears over it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי חייא died before רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא's own words show he outlived רבי.

steps.title: Reverse the names
steps.stepSummary: Answer: flip the names. It was רבי who cried at רבי חייא's grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by switching the names. The real statement was רבי saying he saw רבי חייא's grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא says the speaker and the subject were mixed up. Once flipped, the statement fits with רבי חייא dying first.

phrases.english: Reverse [the names].
phrases.notes: Switch the names: it was רבי who saw רבי חייא's grave and cried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the names in the quoted statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא cried at רבי's grave.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי cried at רבי חייא's grave.

steps.title: Holiness ended the day רבי died
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: רבי חייא said holiness ended on the day רבי died.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי חייא say: On the day רבי died, holiness ceased?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second statement by רבי חייא about רבי's death. This again suggests רבי חייא was alive after רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Speaking about the day someone died implies you lived through that day. So רבי חייא seems to have outlived רבי, against step 26.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ḥiyya say:
On that day that Rabbi died,
holiness ceased!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge of the same kind as step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי חייא died before רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא describes the day of רבי's death, so he was alive then.

steps.title: Reverse the names again
steps.stepSummary: Answer: flip the names. רבי said this about the day רבי חייא died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: switch the names. רבי said holiness ended on the day רבי חייא died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same fix from step 28 is used again. With the names flipped, the statement fits with רבי חייא dying first.

phrases.english: Reverse [the names].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29 the same way step 28 answered step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the names in the quoted statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא said this about רבי's death.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי said this about רבי חייא's death.

steps.title: רבי חייא visits רבי on his sickbed
steps.stepSummary: Challenge from a ברייתא: when רבי fell ill, רבי חייא came in and found him crying.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: When רבי fell ill, רבי חייא came in to him and found him crying. He said to him: רבי, why are you crying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge, this time a story from a ברייתא. It shows רבי חייא at רבי's bedside during his final illness. The story continues in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the source is a ברייתא, not a short statement. It tells a full story with a conversation, showing רבי חייא alive while רבי was dying.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: When Rabbi fell ill,
Rabbi Ḥiyya came in to him
and found him crying.
He said to him: My teacher,
why are you crying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third and stronger challenge to step 26, after steps 28 and 30 answered the first two.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי חייא died before רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows רבי חייא visiting רבי during his final illness, so he was alive at that time.

steps.title: רבי חייא quotes the signs at death
steps.stepSummary: Inside the story, רבי חייא quotes a ברייתא listing good and bad signs at the time of death, including that crying is a bad sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it taught: Dying while laughing is a good sign, while crying is a bad sign. Face up is good, face down is bad. Facing the people is good, facing the wall is bad. A pale face is bad, a bright or ruddy face is good. Dying on ערב שבת is good, on מוצאי שבת is bad. Dying on ערב יום הכפורים is bad, on מוצאי יום הכפורים is good. Dying from a stomach illness is good, because most צדיקים die that way.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still part of the story. רבי חייא backs up his question with a ברייתא: crying at death is a bad sign, so why would רבי cry?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא brings a source to show that crying at death is a bad sign. The full list of signs is quoted, but the key line for him is the first one, about crying.

keyTerms.meaning: the night after (a שבת or holiday ends)

phrases.english: Isn't it taught:
phrases.notes: Now רבי חייא is speaking, quoting a ברייתא to ask why רבי is crying.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת מִתּוֹךְ הַשְּׂחוֹק — סִימָן יָפֶה לוֹ,
phrases.english: One who dies while laughing, it is a good sign for him;
while crying, it is a bad sign for him.
His face upward, it is a good sign for him;
his face downward, it is a bad sign for him.

phrases.aramaic: פָּנָיו כְּלַפֵּי הָעָם — סִימָן יָפֶה לוֹ,
phrases.english: His face toward the people, it is a good sign for him;
toward the wall, it is a bad sign for him.
His face pale, it is a bad sign for him;

phrases.aramaic: פָּנָיו צְהוּבִּין וַאֲדוּמִּים — סִימָן יָפֶה לוֹ.
phrases.english: his face bright and ruddy, it is a good sign for him.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת — סִימָן יָפֶה לוֹ.
phrases.english: One who dies on Shabbat eve, it is a good sign for him.
At the end of Shabbat, it is a bad sign for him.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת בְּעֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים — סִימָן רַע לוֹ,
phrases.english: One who dies on the eve of Yom Kippur, it is a bad sign for him;

phrases.aramaic: בְּמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים — סִימָן יָפֶה לוֹ.
phrases.english: at the end of Yom Kippur, it is a good sign for him.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת מֵחוֹלִי מֵעַיִים — סִימָן יָפֶה לוֹ,
phrases.english: One who dies from an intestinal illness, it is a good sign for him,
because most of the righteous
die from intestinal illness.

steps.confusionAlert: This list of signs is not the גמרא's own challenge. It is רבי חייא speaking inside the story, explaining why he is surprised that רבי is crying.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of step 31; רבי חייא supports his question with a source.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי's crying seems to be a bad sign
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing good and bad signs at death, starting with crying as a bad sign

steps.title: רבי cries over Torah and מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that he is crying over the Torah and מצוות he will no longer be able to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am crying over Torah and מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי explains that his crying is not a bad sign. He is sad to leave the world where a person can learn Torah and do מצוות. This ends the story; the גמרא will answer the challenge next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the story, רבי's answer explains his tears. For the sugya, the main point is that the whole conversation places רבי חייא at רבי's deathbed. That still contradicts step 26.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא said רבי חייא died before רבי. Two statements were answered by switching the names. This ברייתא, which shows רבי חייא talking with the dying רבי, is a third challenge. The next two steps answer it.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רבי is answering רבי חייא.

phrases.english: I am crying over Torah and מצוות!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא אַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת קָא בָכֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חייא's question from steps 31-32 and completes the ברייתא used as a challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is רבי crying, if crying at death is a bad sign?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is crying because he will lose the chance to keep Torah and מצוות.

steps.title: First answer: flip the names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the ברייתא by flipping the names: it was רבי who visited a dying רבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: flip it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the ברייתא about the sickbed visit by flipping the names, just as it did in step 30.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to show that רבי חייא was still alive when רבי was dying. If we flip the names, רבי was the visitor and רבי חייא was the one dying. Then everything fits with the idea that רבי חייא died first.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; it introduces one of several possible answers
Flip it; switch the names in the story

phrases.english: If you wish, say: reverse it,
phrases.notes: Flip who was who: רבי came to visit רבי חייא, not the other way around.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in steps 31-33 by reusing the name-flip from step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the names in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that רבי חייא outlived רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read the story with the names switched, so רבי חייא died first.

steps.title: Second answer: רבי חייא was busy with מצוות
steps.stepSummary: Keep the names as they are. רבי did not appoint רבי חייא as head because רבי חייא was busy with מצוות, and רבי did not want to hold him back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: really, do not flip it. רבי חייא was busy with מצוות, and רבי thought: I will not hold him back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that leaves the sources exactly as they are. רבי חייא was alive, but רבי deliberately chose not to appoint him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We no longer need to say that רבי חייא had died. He was passed over because he was busy with מצוות. Making him head of the ישיבה would have taken him away from that work.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually. It keeps the original reading
I will not hold him back or stop him

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying that רבי חייא was less worthy of the position. It says the opposite: his work for the community was too important to interrupt.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: actually, do not reverse it,
Rabbi Ḥiyya was occupied with מצוות,
and Rabbi thought: I will not hold him back.
phrases.notes: He means: I won't pull him away from his מצוות by making him head of the ישיבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer instead of flipping the names.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason that keeps the sources unchanged
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא must have died, or he would have been appointed.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא was alive but was purposely left free to do his מצוות.

steps.title: רבי חנינא's boast during an argument
steps.stepSummary: This begins a story that shows רבי חייא's מצוות. When רבי חנינא and רבי חייא argued, רבי חנינא said he could rebuild a forgotten תורה through his sharp reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what happened when רבי חנינא and רבי חייא argued. רבי חנינא said to רבי חייא: You argue with me? If, Heaven forbid, the תורה were forgotten from ישראל, I could bring it back through my sharp reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a story to show which מצוות kept רבי חייא so busy. In this first part, רבי חנינא boasts about his own strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and this is' connect the story to the second answer in step 35. רבי חנינא's claim is that his skill in reasoning could rebuild the whole תורה. This sets up the contrast with רבי חייא's reply.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is; it connects a story or saying to what was just said

phrases.english: And this is when they would argue,
Rabbi Ḥanina and Rabbi Ḥiyya,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said to Rabbi Ḥiyya:
You are arguing with me?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם נִשְׁתַּכְּחָה תּוֹרָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: For if, Heaven forfend, the Torah were forgotten from Israel,
I would restore it through my analyses.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּכִי הֲווֹ מִינְּצוּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that backs up the claim that רבי חייא was busy with מצוות.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי חייא was busy with מצוות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the argument between רבי חנינא and רבי חייא

steps.title: רבי חייא's plan to keep the תורה from being forgotten
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that he makes sure the תורה is never forgotten in the first place. He did everything himself: he planted flax, made nets, caught deer, fed orphans, wrote scrolls, and taught children who would then teach each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to him: I make sure the תורה is not forgotten from ישראל. I bring flax and plant it, weave nets, trap deer, feed the meat to orphans, and make scrolls from the deer skins. I go up to a town with no teacher of children. I write the five חומשים for five children and teach the six סדרים of משנה to six children. To each one I say: Teach your part to your friend.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers רבי חנינא's boast. He describes the מצוות that kept him busy, which is the proof for step 35.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא could rebuild the תורה after it was lost. רבי חייא works so it is never lost at all. He makes every part himself, from the flax to the scroll. Each child learns one part and then teaches it to the others, so the whole town ends up knowing all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Flax, a plant used to make thread
The five books of the תורה
The six orders of the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the second answer in step 35. This is the work of מצוות that רבי did not want to interrupt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא עֲבַדִי דְּלָא מִשְׁתַּכְחָה תּוֹרָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: I act so that the Torah will not be forgotten from Israel.
For I bring flax and plant it,
and I weave nets,
and I trap deer,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letter in round brackets; either way the word means deer.

phrases.english: and I feed the meat to orphans,
and I prepare scrolls from the skins of the deer,

phrases.aramaic: וְסָלֵיקְנָא לְמָתָא דְּלֵית בַּהּ מַקְרֵי דַרְדְּקֵי,
phrases.english: and I go up to a town that has no teacher of children,
and I write the five books of the Torah for five children,
and I teach the six orders to six children,
to each and every one I say:
Teach your order to your friend.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא: אֲנָא עֲבַדִי דְּלָא מִשְׁתַּכְחָה תּוֹרָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי חייא's reply to רבי חנינא's boast in step 36.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא was busy with great מצוות
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's own description of how he taught תורה to children

steps.title: רבי says רבי חייא's deeds are greater than his own
steps.stepSummary: רבי praised how great רבי חייא's deeds were. When his son רבי שמעון asked, 'Even greater than yours?', רבי said yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי said: How great are the deeds of חייא! רבי שמעון, the son of רבי, said to him: Even greater than yours? He said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא links רבי's famous praise to the story about רבי חייא. This shows that רבי himself valued these מצוות very highly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי said these deeds were greater than his own, it makes sense that he would not want to stop them. This supports the second answer in step 35.

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi said:
How great are the deeds of Ḥiyya.
Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, said to him:
Even greater than yours?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי: כַּמָּה גְּדוֹלִים מַעֲשֵׂה חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects רבי's praise to the deeds described in step 37.
steps.raayaObject: רבי valued רבי חייא's מצוות above his own
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's saying 'How great are the deeds of חייא'

steps.title: But not greater than רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל, the son of רבי יוסי, asked whether רבי חייא's deeds were greater even than his father's. רבי answered: Heaven forbid, such a thing should not be said in ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוסי said to him: Even greater than my father? He said: Heaven forbid! Such a thing should not be said in ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a limit on the praise. רבי חייא's deeds were greater than רבי's own, but רבי would not say they were greater than רבי יוסי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי was willing to rank רבי חייא above himself. He refused to rank anyone above the great earlier sage רבי יוסי. The praise of רבי חייא is huge, but it still has a limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Such a thing should not be said in ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: There were two answers for why רבי חייא was not made head of the ישיבה. One is to flip the names, so he died first. The other is that he was busy with huge מצוות, especially making sure the תורה would never be forgotten. רבי ranked these deeds above his own, but not above those of רבי יוסי.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, said to him:
Even greater than my father?
He said to him: Heaven forfend,
such a thing should not be said in Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֲפִילּוּ מֵאַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the conversation from step 38 and puts a limit on רבי's praise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא's deeds were greater than רבי's own, but not greater than רבי יוסי's.

steps.title: רבי calls his younger son and gives him wisdom
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks for his younger son, רבי שמעון, and hands him the 'orders of wisdom.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to them: I need my younger son. רבי שמעון came in, and רבי handed him the orders of wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: After the side story about רבי חייא, the גמרא returns to רבי's deathbed instructions. Now he calls his younger son, רבי שמעון, and gives him his last teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each son gets a different gift. The younger son, רבי שמעון, receives 'orders of wisdom,' meaning guidance in Torah and in how to live. This sets up a contrast with the older son, who in the next step receives the leadership.

keyTerms.meaning: He handed over to him / passed on to him
The orders of wisdom: guidance in Torah and in how to conduct oneself

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: לִבְנִי קָטָן אֲנִי צָרִיךְ.
phrases.english: He said to them: I need my younger son.
Rabbi Shimon came in to him,
and he handed over to him the orders of wisdom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: לִבְנִי קָטָן אֲנִי צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about רבי חייא and returns to רבי's deathbed instructions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי passes the 'orders of wisdom' to his younger son, רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבי gives leadership to his older son and tells him to be firm
steps.stepSummary: רבי passes the role of נשיא to רבן גמליאל and tells him to lead firmly and make the students fear him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I need my older son. רבן גמליאל came in, and רבי handed him the ways of being נשיא. He told him: My son, run your time as נשיא with a strong hand, and put fear into the students.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי calls his older son, רבן גמליאל, and hands him the job of נשיא. He gives him one key piece of advice: lead with authority and make the students fear you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The older son gets the leadership, not just wisdom. רבי's advice is to be firm and commanding, not soft. This advice is what the גמרא will challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The procedures of the נשיא's office, how to lead the Jewish people
With loftiness, with a strong and commanding manner
Literally 'throw bile.' It means to put fear into someone

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: לִבְנִי גָּדוֹל אֲנִי צָרִיךְ.
phrases.english: He said to them: I need my older son.
Rabban Gamliel came in to him,
and he handed over to him the procedures of being נשיא.
He said to him: My son, run your time as נשיא with a high hand,
phrases.notes: 'With a high hand' means acting with authority and confidence, not timidly.

phrases.english: throw fear into the students.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: לִבְנִי גָּדוֹל אֲנִי צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 40: after the younger son, now the older son gets his instructions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נשיא should lead with a firm hand and make the students fear him.

steps.title: Challenge: King יהושפט showed warmth to Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי could advise harshness, when יהושפט the king would stand up for, hug and kiss תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But it is written: 'He honors those who fear ה׳,' and the Master said this refers to יהושפט, king of יהודה. When he saw a Torah scholar, he would stand up from his throne, hug him, kiss him, and call him: My teacher, my teacher, my master, my master!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי's advice to be harsh with students. It brings a פסוק and a teaching showing that even a king treated Torah scholars with love and honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said a leader should make the students fear him. But יהושפט, a king who was even higher than a נשיא, rose from his throne and hugged scholars. So it seems a leader should show warmth, not fear.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? A word that opens a challenge

phrases.english: Is that so?
But it is written: 'And he honors those who fear ה׳,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר מָר: זֶה יְהוֹשָׁפָט מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: and the Master said: This is יהושפט, king of יהודה.
When he would see a Torah scholar,
he would stand up from his throne,
and hug him and kiss him,

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹרֵא לוֹ: רַבִּי רַבִּי, מָרִי מָרִי!
phrases.english: and call him: My teacher, my teacher, my master, my master!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי's advice from step 41.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's instruction 'זרוק מרה בתלמידים': put fear into the students.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יהושפט, a king, treated scholars with love and honor. That suggests a leader should be warm toward scholars, not frightening.

steps.title: Warmth in private, firmness in public
steps.stepSummary: Both are correct: show love in private, and keep a firm, commanding manner in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. This one is in private, and that one is in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying both approaches are right, each in its own setting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושפט's hugging and kissing is how a leader should act in private. רבי's advice to be firm is for public settings, where the leader must keep his authority. So the two sources talk about different situations and do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: A leader of Torah should be warm and loving toward scholars in private, but strong and commanding in public.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is in private, that one is in public.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is יהושפט's warmth, which belongs in private. 'That one' is רבי's firmness, which belongs in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּצִינְעָא, הָא בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 42 by dividing between two settings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי's advice to be firm clashed with יהושפט's warm treatment of scholars.
steps.terutzMaskana: Warmth is for private moments, and firmness is for public ones, so both are correct.

steps.title: רבי lay ill in צִיפּוֹרִי, with a burial place ready in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that רבי lay ill in צִיפּוֹרִי, and a burial place was ready for him in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי was lying ill in צִיפּוֹרִי, and a place was prepared for him in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives two facts about רבי's last days: where he lay sick and where he would be buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different towns appear here: רבי was sick in צִיפּוֹרִי but would be buried in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים. This raises a question about where רבי actually lived, and the גמרא picks it up in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: צִיפּוֹרִי, a town in the גליל
בֵּית שְׁעָרִים, a town in the גליל and the seat of רבי's court
A prepared place (here, a burial site)

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi was lying ill in Tzippori,
and a place was ready for him in Beit She'arim.
phrases.notes: The "place" here means his burial spot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the account of רבי's final days with a ברייתא about where he lay and where he would be buried.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי lay ill in צִיפּוֹרִי, and his burial place was prepared in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים.

steps.title: But רבי's court was in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא with a different ברייתא, which shows that רבי was based in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים, not צִיפּוֹרִי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But another ברייתא teaches: "Justice, justice shall you follow" means follow רבי to בֵּית שְׁעָרִים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא. Another ברייתא says to go to רבי's court in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים, so how could he have been lying in צִיפּוֹרִי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא reads the פסוק as telling people to bring their cases to the best court, and it names רבי's court in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים. That shows רבי lived in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים. So it seems he should have been lying ill there, not in צִיפּוֹרִי.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: "Justice, justice shall you follow":
follow Rabbi to Beit She'arim!
phrases.notes: He means: take your case to רבי's court, which sat in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of step 44 with a ברייתא that places רבי in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי lay ill in צִיפּוֹרִי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי's court and home were in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים, so it seems he would have been lying ill there, not in צִיפּוֹרִי.

steps.title: רבי lived in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים but was moved to צִיפּוֹרִי when ill
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי did live in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים, but when he became ill they moved him to צִיפּוֹרִי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי was in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים, but once he became weak, they brought him to צִיפּוֹרִי,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both ברייתות are true: רבי's home was in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים, but he was moved to צִיפּוֹרִי once he fell ill. The reason for the move continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer splits the time: before his illness, רבי was in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים, and during his illness, he was in צִיפּוֹרִי. So the two sources do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: They brought him, they moved him

phrases.english: Rabbi was in Beit She'arim,
but once he became ill,
they brought him to Tzippori,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי בְּבֵית שְׁעָרִים הֲוָה, אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דַּחֲלַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 45 by explaining that רבי was moved from one town to the other.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both sources are true at different times: רבי lived in one town and was moved to the other when he fell ill.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי's court was in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים, he must have been lying ill there.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי lived in בֵּית שְׁעָרִים, but during his illness he was moved to צִיפּוֹרִי.
